subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Bauhaus design movement is best known for promoting:
options: The principle that form follows function with clean, geometric design
questions.explain: The Bauhaus united art, craft and industry around functional, geometric, machine-suited design.

questions.q: The systems approach to manufacturing analyses a process in terms of:
options: Inputs, processes and outputs with feedback
questions.explain: A systems approach models manufacture as inputs, transforming processes and outputs, with feedback for control.

questions.q: User-centred design (UCD) places at the heart of the process:
options: The needs, wants and limitations of the end user
questions.explain: UCD continuously involves and prioritises the end user throughout the design process.

questions.q: Modernism in design emphasised:
options: Mass-produced functional objects stripped of unnecessary ornament
questions.explain: Modernism embraced new materials and machine production with rational, functional, ornament-free forms.

questions.q: A Gore-Tex-style technical textile is described as breathable yet waterproof because its membrane:
options: Has pores too small for water droplets but large enough for water vapour
questions.explain: The microporous membrane lets vapour escape while keeping liquid water out, giving breathable waterproofing.

questions.q: Forging improves the strength of a metal component primarily by:
options: Melting and pouring it into a mould
Compressing and deforming the metal to refine and align its grain structure
questions.explain: Forging plastically deforms metal, refining the grain flow to produce a stronger part than casting.

questions.q: Planned obsolescence is a strategy in which products are:
options: Sold without any warranty by law
Designed to last as long as technically possible
Deliberately designed with a limited useful life to encourage replacement
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence intentionally limits product lifespan to drive repeat purchases.

questions.q: The 95th percentile is used in anthropometric design when a feature must:
options: Suit the smallest users, e.g. reach distances
Accommodate large users, e.g. doorway or seat clearance
questions.explain: The 95th percentile sizes clearances so that large users are accommodated, e.g. headroom or seat width.

questions.q: A Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) evaluates a product's environmental impact:
options: From raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal
Only at the point of sale
questions.explain: LCA is a cradle-to-grave analysis of environmental impact across the entire product life.

questions.q: Quality assurance differs from quality control in that QA is concerned with:
options: Sorting good products from bad after manufacture
Designing the systems and procedures to prevent defects occurring
Inspecting and rejecting faulty finished parts
questions.explain: Quality assurance builds prevention into processes, whereas quality control inspects products against a standard.

questions.q: Design for Disassembly (DfD) primarily supports sustainability by:
options: Making products impossible to take apart
Enabling components to be easily separated for repair, reuse or recycling
Reducing the number of recyclable materials used
questions.explain: DfD allows easy separation of parts and materials at end-of-life for recovery and recycling.

questions.q: Glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) is classified as a composite because it:
options: Is a thermoplastic that can be remelted
Combines glass fibres with a polymer matrix to gain enhanced properties
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more materials—here glass fibres and resin—to achieve superior strength-to-weight properties.

questions.q: The iterative design process is best described as:
options: A repeating cycle of designing, modelling, testing and refining
A single linear sequence completed once
questions.explain: Iterative design repeatedly loops through prototyping and testing to progressively improve a solution.

questions.q: CIM (Computer Integrated Manufacturing) refers to:
options: The use of computers to control and integrate the entire manufacturing process
questions.explain: CIM links CAD, CAM and business systems so computers coordinate the whole production operation.

questions.q: Electroluminescent material is best described as a smart material that:
options: Emits light when an electric current is applied
questions.explain: Electroluminescent materials glow when a voltage is applied across them, used in flexible displays and safety wear.

questions.q: Design for Manufacture (DfM) aims to:
options: Simplify and standardise a design so it is cheaper and easier to produce
Make products as complex as possible
Increase the number of unique parts
questions.explain: DfM optimises a design for efficient, economical and reliable manufacture, often by reducing part count.

questions.q: MDF is an engineered board that is manufactured by:
options: Gluing thin veneers at right angles
Bonding fine wood fibres with resin under heat and pressure
questions.explain: Medium-density fibreboard is made from compressed wood fibres and resin, giving a smooth uniform board.

questions.q: Designing a product to be repairable rather than disposable primarily supports which of the 6 Rs?
questions.explain: Making products serviceable and fixable embodies the 'Repair' principle, extending useful life.

questions.q: Which of these is a thermosetting polymer?
questions.explain: Urea-formaldehyde cures permanently and is a thermoset; the others are thermoplastics.

questions.q: Which property describes a material's ability to be drawn into a wire?
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability to undergo tensile deformation, such as being drawn into wire, without fracturing.

questions.q: Continuous production is characterised by:
options: Running 24/7 to produce identical products without interruption
Making products in limited identical groups
questions.explain: Continuous production runs non-stop, typical of chemicals or float glass, to make a constant flow of product.

questions.q: CAM (Computer Aided Manufacture) most directly involves:
options: Using computer-controlled machines such as CNC routers to make parts
questions.explain: CAM uses software to drive CNC machinery that fabricates a designed part.

questions.q: New and emerging technologies such as automation can impact employment by:
options: Reducing some routine manual roles while creating demand for new technical skills
Having no effect on the workforce
Eliminating the need for any human input ever
questions.explain: Automation displaces routine tasks but generates new roles requiring different, often higher, technical skills.

questions.q: Rotational moulding is particularly suited to producing:
options: Large hollow seamless items such as water tanks and kayaks
questions.explain: Rotational moulding coats the inside of a rotating heated mould to form large seamless hollow products.

questions.q: Consumer protection legislation (e.g. the Consumer Rights Act) requires goods to be:
options: Of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described
questions.explain: Consumer law requires that goods are of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and match their description.

questions.q: The British Standards Institution (BSI) Kitemark indicates that a product:
options: Has been independently tested to meet a recognised standard of safety/quality
questions.explain: The Kitemark is a BSI certification mark showing a product meets a defined standard.

questions.q: A dimension specified as 50 mm +/-0.2 mm has a tolerance whose limits are:
questions.explain: The bilateral tolerance of +/-0.2 mm gives an upper limit of 50.2 mm and a lower limit of 49.8 mm.

questions.q: Ergonomics is concerned with:
options: Designing products to fit the user's body, capabilities and comfort
The cost of raw materials only
questions.explain: Ergonomics studies the interaction between people and products to optimise comfort, safety and efficiency.

questions.q: Industry 4.0 is most associated with:
options: The first use of steam power
Cyber-physical systems, IoT data and smart automated factories
questions.explain: Industry 4.0 describes the fourth industrial revolution of interconnected smart machines, IoT and data analytics.

questions.q: An alloy is best defined as:
options: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements to improve properties
questions.explain: Alloys combine a base metal with other elements—e.g. steel is iron and carbon—to enhance properties.
